scenario.description: A product director must approve the production rollout configuration for a redesigned bulk-invoice export workflow, including the initial cohort, concurrency limit, retry behavior, download retention, and support process, after the standard launch review.

shared_context.S1: The redesigned bulk-invoice export workflow is planned for its first production rollout next Monday.
shared_context.S2: The workflow passed the planned staging tests and completed a pilot with 20 internal accounts.
shared_context.S3: The current launch draft proposes enabling the feature for all customers, allowing up to 50 concurrent exports, retrying after 5 seconds, and retaining completed downloads for 1 day.
shared_context.S4: Taylor makes the final rollout call, and the standard launch review includes a check-in with customer operations and data engineering before the configuration is finalized.

PF1.text: While reviewing account-support procedures for another launch this morning, Riley confirmed that the enterprise order forms for four named customers require bulk-invoice downloads to remain available for 7 days; the support playbook has not been updated because the contract review finished only an hour ago.

PF2.text: During an unrelated queue-capacity investigation this afternoon, Morgan measured that production can safely sustain exactly 12 concurrent exports, and that retries need a 30-second backoff; Morgan also recommends starting with exactly 25 percent of customers to keep queue growth within the observed limit, but has not yet filed the capacity note.

acceptance_conditions: The initial rollout must be exactly 25 percent of customers.
The workflow must be limited to exactly 12 concurrent exports.
Automatic retries must use a 30-second backoff.
Completed downloads must be retained for exactly 7 days.
A customer-support playbook update commitment must be recorded.
A production-capacity monitoring commitment must be recorded.

content_checks.C5: any(('support playbook' in c['detail'] or 'Support playbook' in c['detail']) and c['target'] in ['Riley', 'customer operations'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(('capacity note' in c['detail'] or 'Capacity note' in c['detail']) and c['target'] in ['Morgan', 'data engineering'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The contract confirmation changes download retention from the draft's 1 day to exactly 7 days and creates the support-playbook update commitment.
The production queue measurement changes the rollout to exactly 25 percent, concurrency to exactly 12, retry backoff to exactly 30 seconds, and adds the capacity-monitoring commitment.
